name: DES Year 3 cosmological constraints from galaxy clustering and weak lensing
notes: The paper title says "Year 3 Results"; the abstract calls it "the first cosmology results from large-scale structure in the Dark Energy Survey (DES) spanning 5000 deg2".

summary.plain: The first cosmology results from the Dark Energy Survey's large-scale structure, from its first three years of data over 5000 square degrees. Combining cosmic shear, galaxy clustering and galaxy-galaxy lensing, DES finds a clustering amplitude consistent with the Planck-favoured model.
summary.technical: DES Y3 3×2pt analysis (100 million source galaxies): S8 = 0.776 ± 0.017 and Ωm = 0.339 (+0.032, -0.031) in ΛCDM; S8 = 0.775 (+0.026, -0.024), Ωm = 0.352 (+0.035, -0.041) and w = -0.98 (+0.32, -0.20) in wCDM; consistent with Planck 2018 (probability-to-exceed p = 0.13 to 0.48). Combined with BAO, RSD, SNe Ia and Planck lensing: Σmν < 0.13 eV (95% CL).

title: Dark Energy Survey Year 3 Results: Cosmological Constraints from Galaxy Clustering and Weak Lensing
why_it_matters: The abstract says the DES data are consistent with the prediction of the model favoured by Planck 2018 CMB primary anisotropy data, quantified by a probability-to-exceed p = 0.13 to 0.48.
